fieldValues.title: What counts as a recorded ruling for a group's mandate
fieldValues.decision_question: Which records count as a recorded ruling when WG Third-party ready decides an issue is inside its mandate ('executes a recorded ruling, RFC or invariant and names it')?
fieldValues.context:
Problem: the 2026-10-20 triage of the group's 63 parked issues found the same question deciding about one in six of them. The group's analyst may unpark only ruling-backed work, but the authority behind much of the backlog is not an rfc-decision record:
- the relation principles R1-R11 live in design-note 044, ratified 2026-07-14 through the srs#171 epic, with no rfc-decision record (srs-rust#557, srs-vscode#45, srs#180, srs#181);
- the capability-layering rules R5 and R6 are stated as ratified in srs-rust/docs/architecture/capability-layering.md only (srs-web#407, #216, #167);
- the implementation ADRs (ADR-041, ADR-042, ADR-048, ADR-053, ADR-011) name deferred work exactly (srs-rust#704, #725-#731, #1147, #1342, #1343, #601);
- some owner rulings exist only in issue threads (srs#883, srs-rust#813, #688).
The triage counted ADR-011 and ADR-053 (they name the exact work) and nothing else, so 20 issues stay KEEP.
Why it matters: answers SP-02 (rulings are made but never executed). A ruling that the group cannot cite cannot be executed by it, and the backlog stays parked while the queue runs dry (3 ready against a budget of 10).
Options and consequences: (a) only rfc-decision records, accepted RFC requirements and spec invariants count; design-note 044, R5/R6 and thread rulings are first promoted into rfc-decision records (a spec act, through the RFC process); ADRs never count. (b) As (a) for spec-side work, plus accepted srs-rust ADRs count for implementation-side work in srs-rust that changes no CLI or payload contract; thread rulings are recorded as decisions first (D11). (c) Anything the owner has ruled, wherever it is written, counts. (d) Do nothing: the analyst stays conservative and these issues stay parked.
Recommendation: (b), with design-note 044 R1-R11 and R5/R6 promoted into rfc-decision records as the first spec work it creates.
Action needed: ratify in a session; then the analyst re-runs the triage against the ratified rule and updates routines/wg-analyst.md section 3 ('Mandate').
Urgency: medium. It decides the group's next queue.
fieldValues.friction: Three triage agents independently flagged the same question in srs, srs-rust and the clients on 2026-10-20.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
(a) Spec records only. Leads to one source of authority and a short spec workload before about ten issues can move. Leans to Office over Testimony.
(b) Spec records for the spec; accepted ADRs for implementation-internal work. Leads to the storage-refactor family and #1147 moving at once, while contract changes still need the spec. Follows the layer rule: implementation decisions live in srs-rust ADRs (ADR-048).
(c) Any owner ruling. Leads to the most work moving, with authority that cannot be traced to a record.
(d) Do nothing. Leads to the queue staying dry and the backlog parked.
fieldValues.key_requirements: Whatever counts must be citable by id in the issue's Ruling line, and traceable to a ratified record. No rule may let an agent widen its own mandate.
fieldValues.decision_statement: For WG Third-party ready, a recorded ruling is an rfc-decision record, an accepted RFC requirement or a spec invariant; for implementation-internal work in srs-rust that changes no CLI, payload or WASM contract, an accepted srs-rust ADR also counts. An owner ruling written anywhere else is recorded as a decision before it is cited.
fieldValues.rationale: Authority should be traceable to a record at the layer it governs: spec rulings in the spec, implementation rulings in the implementation's ADRs. Promoting R1-R11 and R5/R6 closes the gap where both sides already cite them as ratified.
fieldValues.revisit_when: The next triage of the group's parked issues, or when an ADR-backed change is found to have altered a contract a third party relies on.
